- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py: lines 482-486 (_blocked_label_targets MCP branch) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The MCP branch in _blocked_label_targets checks that BLOCKED_LABEL is in the labels list but does not inspect the method field of the mcp__*__issue_write tool input. The Bash branch at lines 488-490 explicitly checks call["method"] == "POST". The MCP path at line 482-486 has no equivalent guard.
  WHY: If an MCP issue_write with a method other than "update" (e.g. "delete" or "create") passes a labels list containing ai:claude-blocked — for example as the current state or the to-be-created labels — the hook would count a label removal or a label-on-new-issue as a verified blocker label addition. The comment result is verified via its URL, but the label result is only checked for is_error, so a non-error delete or create result would satisfy the label-write requirement without ever adding the label to the marker's issue. The test helper _mcp_label always sets method: "update", so this path has zero test coverage for non-update methods.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py: lines 265-272 (_contains_marker definition) | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: _contains_marker is defined but has zero callers after the rewrite of blocked_comment_posted. The old blocked_comment_posted called it to scan tool inputs for the marker string anywhere in the value. The new implementation uses _blocked_comment_targets, _starts_with_marker, and _blocked_label_targets instead. The only references to _contains_marker are its own recursive calls on lines 269 and 271.
  WHY: No runtime failure — this is dead code. In a security hook that already had a finding (forged-blocked-comment-evidence) from its last review, dead code implementing the old, weaker marker-anywhere check may mislead future readers into thinking that check is still active alongside the new verified-blocker check.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py (and the workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py twin, byte-identical on this head): _blocked_label_targets, MCP branch (around lines 482-486) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The MCP branch of _blocked_label_targets only checks that BLOCKED_LABEL is in tool_input["labels"] and that the issue target resolves to the marker. It never inspects tool_input["method"]. The Bash branch immediately above it guards with `call["method"] == "POST"`, which is why the existing test_other_bash_shapes_do_not_count entry `"gh api -X DELETE repos/.../labels -f 'labels[]=ai:claude-blocked'"` is correctly rejected. No such guard exists on the MCP side, and there is no test exercising a non-"update" MCP method either.
  WHY: If `mcp__github__issue_write` (or any future `*__issue_write` MCP tool that ends with the MCP_LABEL_TOOL_SUFFIX constant) accepts a method other than "update" — most plausibly "delete" — that takes a labels list and removes those labels from the existing issue, an unattended session could call it with `method: "delete"`, `labels: ["ai:claude-blocked"]`, and `issue_number` set to the marker issue. The hook would record the call as a verified label write on the marker issue (the label-result branch is a bare non-error check; it does not verify the response URL the way the comment branch does), the tool would actually strip the existing blocker label, and the session would be free to end its turn on a question after silently removing the very label the hook is supposed to require. The asymmetry is concrete: the plan (AD-6) explicitly only considered `gh api` shapes and the label-write response is unverifiable beyond non-error, so the MCP path was under-defended by design.
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py (and the workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py twin, byte-identical on this head): _contains_marker, lines 265-272 (definition retained verbatim from the pre-rewrite file) | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: After the rewrite of blocked_comment_posted, _contains_marker(value) has zero callers anywhere in the hook or in tests/test_unattended_question_guard.py. The old blocked_comment_posted called `_contains_marker(item.get("input"))` to scan tool call inputs for the marker string anywhere in the value; the new blocked_comment_posted uses _starts_with_marker, _blocked_comment_targets, and _blocked_label_targets instead, and `_contains_marker` is never referenced again. The symbol-level diff listing for _contains_marker names the file itself and the plan markdown as "callers", but those are references in prose / the definition site, not invocations.
